questions.q: What does the Scheduled Path in this lab's flow do?
options: Lets the flow come back and re-check the Case 4 hours after it was created, rather than only at creation
Runs the flow immediately whenever the Case is created
Deletes the Case if it's still open after 4 hours
Converts the Case into a Lead automatically
questions.explain: A Scheduled Path is a record-triggered flow branch that runs at a set offset from the trigger event — here, 4 hours after the Case's CreatedDate.

questions.q: What does the 'Still Open and Unescalated?' Decision check?
options: Whether the Case has more than 5 comments
Whether Status is not Closed and Escalated__c is still False
Whether the related Account is a customer
Whether the Case owner is active
questions.explain: This Decision determines whether the case still genuinely needs escalation — not closed, and not already flagged as escalated.

questions.q: What does the loop over teamMembers do in this flow, and what does it deliberately NOT do?
options: It sends an individual email to each team member as it loops
It deletes team members who haven't responded
It updates each team member's profile
It only collects each team member's email address into a collection variable — it never sends anything itself
questions.explain: Following the bulkification pattern, the loop's only job is building emailCollection — the actual Send Email action happens once, outside the loop.

questions.q: Why does the Send Email Action sit outside the loop instead of inside it?
options: Flow Builder doesn't allow Action elements inside loops
It has no effect either way on performance
Putting it inside the loop would fire one separate email send per team member instead of one send to the whole collection — the exact unbulkified pattern from Lesson 22
Outside the loop, the email can only go to the Case owner
questions.explain: An Action element inside a loop re-runs once per item, just like a DML element would — moving it outside and sending to the whole collection at once avoids that.

questions.q: What does the fault path off Send Email do in this after-save flow?
options: It blocks the Case from being saved
It automatically resends the email up to 10 times
It deactivates the flow
It creates a Flow_Error__c record with the real error message and a link back to the Case, since a notification failure here can't block the save itself
questions.explain: Since this flow runs after save, a failed notification can't block the Case — but the fault path still logs the real $Flow.FaultMessage to a dedicated record instead of failing silently.
